<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="BRPXQZME" />{{running header|398|{{asc|THE SHIH KING.}}|{{smaller|{{asc|DECADE II.}}}}}}{{rule}}</noinclude>When he was able to crawl,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He looked majestic and intelligent.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
When he was able to feed himself,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He fell to planting beans.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The beans grew luxuriantly;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
His rows of paddy shot up beautifully;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
His hemp and wheat grew strong and close;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
His gourds yielded abundantly.

The husbandry of Hâu-''k''î{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Proceeded on the plan of helping (the growth).{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Having cleared away the thick grass,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He sowed the ground with the yellow cereals.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
He managed the living grain, till it was ready to burst;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Then he used it as seed, and it sprang up;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
It grew and came into ear;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
It became strong and good;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
It hung down, every grain complete;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And thus he was appointed lord of {{tooltip|Thâi|Tái}}<ref>[[w:Hou Ji|Hâu-''k''î]]'s mother, we have seen, was a princess of [[w:Tai (city)|Thâi]], in the present district of [[w:Wugong County|Wû-kung]], [[w:Qian County|''Kh''ien ''K''au]], [[w:Shaanxi|Shen-hsî]]. This may have led to his appointment to that principality, and the transference of the lordship from [[w:Jiāng (surname 姜)|''K''iang]]s to [[w:Ji (Zhou dynasty ancestral surname)|''K''î]]s. Evidently he was appointed to that dignity for his services in the promotion of agriculture. Still he has not displaced the older [[w:Shennong|Shăn-nung]], with whom on his father's side he had a connexion, as 'the Father of Husbandry.'</ref>.

He gave (his people) the beautiful grains;—{{lb}}The
black millet and the double-kernelled,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The tall red and the white.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They planted extensively the black and the double-kernelled,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Which were reaped and stacked on the ground.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
They planted extensively the tall red and the white,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Which were carried on their shoulders and backs,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Home for the sacrifices which he founded<ref>This is not to be understood of sacrifice in general, as if there had been no such thing before [[w:Hou Ji|Hâu-''k''î]]; but of the sacrifices of the of [[Portal:Zhou dynasty|House of ''K''âu]],—those in the [[w:Ancestral temple|ancestral temple]] and others,—which began with him as its great ancestor.</ref>.

And how as to our sacrifices (continued from him)?{{lb}}<noinclude><!--¶-->
